newsitem.title: CANADA: Quebec says on track with government job cuts.
newsitem.headline: Quebec says on track with government job cuts.

text.p: The Quebec government is on track to cut C$1.4 billion from its annual payroll costs, a senior goverment official told the daily newspaper Journal de Quebec on Wednesday.
"We are fairly certain of meeting our objective and we will probably exceed it," Pierre-Judes Polin, spokesman for for Quebec's Treasury Board told the newspaper.
More than 24,000 government employees have indicated they plan to retire by July 1, exceeding the 15,000 target originally set by the government.

According to Quebec's Commission administrative des regimes de retraite et d'assurances (CARRA), in addition to other retirements, more than 2,450 civil servants, 8,410 health care workers, and 7,600 employees of Quebec's junior colleges and school boards will take early retirement on July 1, the newspaper said.
The job cuts are part of the Quebec government's plan to cut C$3.6 billion of expenses from its fiscal 1997/98 budget.
